notes.title: Update #25: Created a Patreon & Optimized code base
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

Quick little update from my side. I’ve been deep in the trenches of code refactoring lately - the core systems are in a pretty solid place now. Most of the heavy groundwork is finished, but once I started testing things together (units, battle units, workers, generals, etc.), the calculations felt a bit clunky. So I rolled up my sleeves and rebuilt some of the core logic to make it more optimized for all the modifiers and interactions that will come into play later. It should run much smoother now as the complexity ramps up.



On a different note: I’ve just launched a Patreon page!


If you’d like to support the development and help me spend more focused time on Quartermaster, that’s the best way to do it.

👉 https://www.patreon.com/cw/FeysStudio


That said - and this is important - even if nobody ever forks over a single dollar, I’ll still finish this game. Quartermaster is a bit of a bucket list project for me, and I’m fully committed to seeing it through. The Patreon just helps me dedicate more hours to it without distraction. If anyone decides it's worth supporting...


Thanks again for following along - your interest and feedback already mean a lot. More updates soon!

notes.title: Update #23&24 - Location stats, tasks and Upgrade system finished
notes.content:
Big Progress Update – Task Systems + Upgrade Framework Live

This week brought two major systems into working shape: Depot Worker Tasks and the Upgrade System. Together, they significantly advance the game’s dynamic structure and open up a lot of design flexibility for future development.
I forgot to post them on here, so both updates at once. The devlog videos at the end of the post.
[hr][/hr]Depot Worker Tasks Completed Across All Locations
Each location now has a distinct task system fully defined and ready. These tasks are tied to the gameplay logic and reflect the core function of the building or area—be it healing troops, storing supplies, or managing animals. Each location also has its own condition and performance stats (e.g., fire safety, pest control, structural decay), which tasks will soon influence in real-time.

Tasks are currently functional but not yet connected to stat changes. That dynamic link—e.g., “more cleaning = less sickness,” or “more maintenance = slower equipment decay”—is next on the implementation list. The framework is fully modular, so expanding, tweaking, or balancing it later will be simple.

Additionally, all location modules are now cleanly declared, stat-modifiable, and trackable. This includes systems like how many vehicles can be repaired in the Mechanics Bay, how many animals can be stabled, and whether the Storage is fire-safe. Upgrade logic is already wired in—each module can now accept upgrades and reflect changes based on worker activity and game state.
[hr][/hr]Upgrade System Fully Implemented
A complete UpgradeProcessor is now in place. This handles the logic of applying upgrades across the game world—whether it's increasing capacity in Storage, adding new delivery types to the Depot, or enhancing a battle unit’s efficiency. Upgrades can now affect all kinds of stats and work exactly like modifiers, but persist across time and can have levels.

The upgrade system includes:

A centralized upgrade definition database

Proper initialization and registration at game start

Support for both static upgrades (e.g., unlock cart access) and scaling upgrades (e.g., +5%, +10%, etc.)

A clean level system for upgrades: rather than duplicating entries, each upgrade has a level property. This lets you scale the effect by level and keep everything manageable for both logic and UI later (e.g., visual differences between Level 1 vs. Level 3 shield upgrades).

Entities now carry upgrade dictionaries and snapshots, just like modifiers. All interaction and logic are contained within processors for clarity and modularity.

I will create and list the different upgrades at a later stage. The core mechanics are more important to me. Once the different core mechanics are finished, I will flesh out the modifier and upgrade list, etc. to take care of balancing issues.
[hr][/hr]Examples of Location Roles and Their Tasks
Here’s a quick overview of what each location is responsible for, plus their assignable worker tasks:

Barracks – Troop rest, morale, readiness
→ Tasks: Cleaning, Maintenance, Construction, Upgrading, Security, Sleeping

Hospital – Medical care, epidemic response
→ Tasks: Medical Help, Cleaning, Maintenance, Inventory, Upgrading, Repair, Security

Mechanics Bay – Repairs trucks, small vehicles
→ Tasks: Repair Units, Cleaning, Maintenance, Inventory, Upgrading, Security

Stables – Houses animals for transport/comms
→ Tasks: Animal Care, Cleaning, Maintenance, Upgrading, Security, Repair

Depot – Central hub for all incoming/outgoing resources
→ Tasks: Loading/Unloading, Maintenance, Construction, Cleaning, Security, Upgrading

Deployment Zone – Infrastructure across the region (rails, lines, bridges)
→ Tasks: Repair, Maintenance, Upgrading, Building, Security

Storage – Stores strategic resources
→ Tasks: Loading, Inventory Management, Cleaning, Maintenance, Security, Upgrading

Sector – Abstract representation of overall theater condition
→ No direct tasks, but heavily affected by all others through modifiers and global conditions.
[hr][/hr]Next Steps
The next big milestone will be the Officer System—commanders who issue missions and exert influence. Officers will impact gameplay via buffs, pressure, and event chains, affecting both unit behavior and strategic choices.

Thanks again to everyone following along and offering feedback. The system is shaping up with a clean architecture, and most elements are already communicating through shared logic, signals, and processors.

notes.title: Update #22: Depot Worker Task Logic finished
notes.content:
Today was a big milestone in the development of Quartermaster! I finally implemented the entire task management logic for our hardworking depot workers.



Now, the game can assign and unassign tasks dynamically or through hand by the player across different areas - whether it’s barracks, the deployment zone, the hospital, the mechanics bay, or beyond. Each worker now has proper stats: you can check exactly which worker is assigned to which task, at which place, and adjust it on the fly.

While the basis is rather simple, making sure no task could be assigned twice, no worker on two assignments and to make sure the code would always know and be able to adapt where exactly which worker exactly is, took a bit of fiddling.



I even got tasks like repairing telegraph lines, upgrading shelters, barracks cleaning, and sleeping already included.



Of course, there’s more to come: I still need to add a few additional tasks for other zones, but the foundational logic is solid. Assigning workers will actually affect game values - things like unloading speed, how fast or slow buildings degrade, how secure the depot is from sabotage, and so on. It’s all dynamic, and it’s going to add a whole new layer of depth to the gameplay.



This was a huge chunk of the logic, and I’m honestly proud to have it finished. It took a lot of careful checking.



Next up: I’ll be expanding the task list for all the different zones. Once that’s in place, the Depot Worker Tasks will be fully fleshed out! After that, I will not immediately implement the modifiers that make their work actually impact the game world (e.g., boosting efficiency, handling maintenance, etc.) and instead think I will first implement the upgrade system for units and modules/zones.



Thanks for following along - and stay tuned for more updates!
